name: Pixpaw
summary: A pixel cat that lives on your desktop and talks to you
description: A little pixel cat lives on your desktop. It wanders the whole screen, just the bottom edge, or the bottom edge and the tops of your open windows, riding along when you move one. It grooms, purrs when you click it, stalks and pounces on files you drag, gets hungry and eats from a bowl you put down. It also tells you things in a speech bubble: notifications from your other apps, calendar events about to start, song changes (and it dances to whatever is playing, YouTube included), your coding agents finishing or needing you, volume and brightness changes, headphones connecting, the battery and finished downloads. It meows, purrs and crunches, reminds you to take breaks, earns happiness points that unlock pixel hats and collars, and can bring a friend along. Hold on it for a menu to feed it, have it nap, or play with a yarn ball, a feather teaser or a laser pointer it never quite catches. Drag it anywhere, pick from six coats on the shelf, and turn on Follow the cursor in its settings to have it chase your pointer. Not a cat person? Pick a bee, a parrot, a dinosaur, a dog, a hamster, a chicken, a giraffe, a hippo, a rabbit or a shark that swims through the air instead, each with its own sounds. On festival days the screen joins in: ghosts on Halloween, fireworks at New Year, snow at Christmas, water drops for Songkran and hearts on Valentine's Day. Stroke it, toss it a treat, take its photo, stretch together, or start a focus session and it works along with you at its own little laptop. Reach 500 stars and it gets a home of its own, after where the animal really lives, to nap in. Or draw your own pet in any pixel editor (one pose is enough), bring it in, give it sounds of its own and pick which character it acts like. Throw it and it bounces off the edges of the screen; now and then it climbs the walls. It types along while you type, codes along while your agents work, sweats when your Mac works hard, holds up a note for you on a little sign, and carries files you drop on it to Droppy's shelf. Its sign is your to-do list too: add notes with a shortcut, and a note with a time brings it over to remind you. Focus in Pomodoro rounds, and it nudges you back if you wander off to YouTube. Click it to join your next video call, count down to the days you're looking forward to on its sign, and have it capture a whole web page, top to bottom, in one tall picture. When Claude Code asks to run something or asks you a question, your pet brings it over and reads it out, with the answers on a card to click. Every animal has a toy of its own (a frisbee for the dog, a carrot for the rabbit, a watermelon for the hippo), dogs play fetch, and now and then your pet play-fights its friend in a cartoon cloud of dust. It poses for your screenshots, welcomes you back, says good morning with your first event of the day, celebrates your birthday with confetti, and after midnight it puts on a nightcap and tells you it's late. The shelf widget counts your days together.
